entries.clue: Scots lassie without golf ball tours royal estate (8)

indicatorNotes.without: to go without something is to lack it, so the G is removed from Morag

annotation.surface: A Scottish girl loses her golf ball somewhere on the royal grounds.
annotation.walkthrough: Golf is G in the NATO alphabet. Balmoral is the royal family's estate in Aberdeenshire, so the Scottish setting helps rather than misleads.
annotation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle and its estate in Scotland are a private home of the British royal family.

entries.clue: Panto character getting leg stuck in barrels (7)

the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

annotation.surface: A pantomime actor gets a leg jammed in some barrels during a slapstick routine.
annotation.walkthrough: Leg = ON is a cricket term: the leg side and the on side are the same half of the field. A panto is a British family Christmas show.
annotation.definitionFit: Buttons is the cheerful page boy in the pantomime Cinderella.

entries.clue: Stout cat tried to bite Lawrence initially (4-7)

a judge tries, or hears, a case

entries.clue: Typically concerning type of road fury (2,7)

read spirits as ghosts: a famous Victorian tale where three Christmas ghosts visit a miser

annotation.definitionFit: A Christmas Carol is Dickens's story of Scrooge and the three Christmas ghosts.

entries.clue: Republican lodging in a bogus religious retreat (6)

indicatorNotes.lodging in: a lodger lives inside someone else's house, so R is put inside A SHAM

entries.clue: An eccentric with Marmite’s generally accepted (10)

indicatorNotes.eccentric: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone with odd tastes finds that Marmite has gone mainstream.
annotation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British yeast spread famous for dividing opinion, which is the joke of calling it generally accepted.
annotation.definitionFit: Mainstream means following the ideas most people accept.

entries.clue: Makeshift fit-looking opener for Essex goes in (7)

entries.clue: Copy current partner importing tech (7)

indicatorNotes.importing: MATE imports IT, taking it inside

entries.clue: Old noble gas knocking out setter (5)

annotation.definitionFit: A thane was a nobleman in Anglo-Saxon England and medieval Scotland, like Macbeth.

entries.clue: After short nap, Joe upset country in leaving of office (11)

indicatorNotes.After: after means coming later, so the other pieces are written after RES

annotation.walkthrough: Joe = GI comes from GI Joe, the nickname for an American soldier.

a machine that is on is working

annotation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a state ruled by a monarch, so a king's domain.

entries.clue: Little bird starts to warble regularly, every night (4)

blocks.clueFragment: starts to warble regularly, every night

annotation.surface: A small bird sings at regular intervals every night.
annotation.walkthrough: "Regularly" usually calls for alternate letters; here it is only one of the words whose first letter is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: The wren is one of the smallest British birds.

entries.clue: Troop carrier starts to roll off Jutland in stormy North Sea (6,5)

annotation.walkthrough: Jutland is the Danish peninsula on the North Sea, so the whole surface is a plausible voyage.
annotation.definitionFit: The Greeks hid soldiers inside the wooden Trojan horse to get them into Troy.

read Genesis as the Bible's first book, which records Adam and Eve's fall, the flaw every human is said to be born with

entries.clue: Earth Switzerland found in mineral deposit (5)

entries.clue: One gram gold coin that’s common (7)

annotation.walkthrough: "Common" looks like widespread; here it is the old sense of low-born, the opposite of noble.

Captain America is one of Marvel's Avengers

annotation.surface: Is the man sweeping the street secretly Captain America?
annotation.walkthrough: SC is short for scilicet, meaning namely. A scavenger was the old name for a street sweeper.
annotation.definitionFit: Scavenger was the historical word for someone employed to clean the streets.

entries.clue: Now and again, she eats key natural condiment (3,4)
